newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - COYOTES JUMP ON BLUES EARLY IN 4-2 VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - COYOTES JUMP ON BLUES EARLY IN 4-2 VICTORY.

text.p: The Phoenix Coyotes scored on their first two shots of the game and Nikolai Khabibulin made 37 saves in a 4-2 victory over the St Louis Blues on Monday.
Keith Tkachuk notched his 34th goal just 33 seconds into the game and Jeremy Roenick drove home the Coyotes' next shot on goal just under two minutes later with Craig Janney setting up both tallies.
"We had some good jump tonight, we really went out and took the play to them early," Roenick said.
Mike Gartner made it 3-0 with his 22nd goal, a powerplay tally at 10:34, as Phoenix victimised Blues goalie Grant Fuhr three times on just seven shots in the first period.
"It looked like the first five minutes we weren't ready to play," St. Louis coach Joel Quenneville said. "It was 2-0 right off the bat before we know we're in the game."

Khabibulin faced nearly twice as many shots as Fuhr as the Blues outshot the Coyotes 39-21. But he turned away all 29 shots over the first two periods before Mike Peluso's goal 7:54 into the final period made it 3-1.
Jamie Rivers also scored for the Blues to cut the lead to 3-2 at 15:34 of the third, but Bob Corkum added an insurance goal for Phoenix with 62 seconds remaining.
In Montreal, rookie goalie Jose Theodore made 47 saves and Vincent Damphousse had a goal and two assists to lead the Canadiens to a 4-2 victory over the San Jose Sharks.
Dody Wood and Steve Guolla scored for San Jose, but Sharks goalie Kelly Hrudey allowed three goals on 11 shots in the first period.
Damphousse scored his 21st goal on a powerplay 6:15 into the game to tie the score at 1-1, wristing in a rebound of a shot by Martin Rucinsky.
Turner Stevenson and Vladimir Malakhov also scored in the first for the Canadiens and Rucinsky added an insurance tally at 13:26 of the third.
Damphousse's assist on Malakhov's goal was the 800th point of his career, a milestone he called "a big deal."
"When I started out, I set goals for myself. I wanted to play 1,000 games and get 1,000 points. I'm getting closer, but I'm also getting older.
"I've been around this league for 11 years. That means that time is getting short."
